Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

pdmS7 (development version)

  • The introductory articles are rewritten in plain English with figures of the model running: “How the PDM works” (buckets, dry and wet ground, the saturated area, the two paths to the river, the water balance, and what each setting does), “How the snow model works” (a winter, rain on snow, snow cover, settings, and snow with the PDM) and “Your first model run” (from data files to a calibrated, saved model). Each ends with a short equations appendix; the new “Model equations” page holds the full reference.
  • New write_pdm_config() writes a configuration that read_pdm_config() reads back exactly; general YAML writers round numbers to seven significant figures.
  • “Calibrating many catchments” is rewritten as a plain-English, step-by-step guide to calibrate_batch(), run live with an interruption and a failure. “Automatic calibration” is rewritten in plain English.
  • New calibrate_batch() runs one calibration protocol on every basin in a folder (each with forcing.csv, flow.csv and basin.yml), giving each basin its own calibration-log project, in parallel with cores. It can be stopped and restarted at any point: each basin carries on from its last completed step and finished steps are never repeated. Failures are recorded with their reason without stopping the batch. batch_status() shows progress from batch-status.csv; batch_results() collects the projects.
  • Three new articles: “Scoring a simulation” (every score, with the contingency table, event matching, events against steps and the performance diagram), “Automatic calibration” (bounds, log-scale search, the two optimisers and threshold objectives) and “Inside the logs” (project folders, entry files, the checksum chain, the run log and the register). The site’s articles are regrouped into Calibration, Records and review, and Forecasting.
  • New compare_structures() calibrates several model structures alike, in parallel with cores, logs each as a structure and an automatic calibration linked by a comparison id, and ranks them on the validation window, with optional two-way cross-validation. structure_comparison() rebuilds a ranking from the log. structure_set() gives the standard PDM and seven one-change variants; calibration_bounds() gives default bounds from inst/calibration-bounds.csv. The report and the app (a new Structures tab) show comparisons.
  • calibrate_pdm() and log_auto_calibration() gain log_scale, searching named parameters uniformly in log(value).
  • register_data() gains an optional test window, scored once by the new test_candidate() entry after every choice is made, and required before sign-off when registered.
  • New article, “Choosing a model structure”.
  • New article, “Calibrating many catchments”: one logged protocol applied to a batch of basins, budgeting, catching failures, judging scores as a distribution, checking whether multi-start runs agreed, and how well calibration recovers known parameters.
  • New read_entry() returns one calibration-log entry in full, and read_projects() gains validation_score, the candidate’s headline score on the validation window.
  • New threshold verification. pdm_threshold_scores() scores one or more thresholds at once: events (episodes above a threshold, merged across short gaps and matched within a timing tolerance) give probability of detection, false alarm ratio, critical success index and frequency bias, plus crossing time, peak timing, peak, duration and volume errors for each hit; a step-by-step count adds probability of false detection, equitable threat score and Peirce skill score.
  • register_data() gains thresholds (flows, or levels converted through a registered rating table and never extrapolated) and event settings. Every logged run is scored at every threshold, and a threshold score such as csi:Flood Warning may be the headline. The report adds a threshold table and a performance diagram.
  • calibrate_pdm() gains method = "nelder_mead", a derivative-free optimiser kept within the bounds, and an optional threshold term in the objective (thresholds, threshold_weight, threshold_score), or objective = "threshold" alone. log_auto_calibration() passes registered thresholds by name and records the method, objective and number of model runs. The default method and objective are unchanged.
  • New article, “Logging a manual calibration”: a complete project from start to sign-off, integrity checks and tampering, the report, and tracing operational runs with the run log.
  • New calibration_app(): a Shiny app over the calibration log for staff who prefer not to script. Setup (start, register data, select structure), Trial (adjust parameters, preview the hydrograph and scorecard against the parent, save with a verdict and reasoning; notes; automatic calibration), History (path, every run, compare two runs, propose and validate a candidate), Report (integrity, build and download) and Sign-off. Every button calls the exported function a script would, so the same rules apply. shiny is a suggested package, needed only for the app.
  • New opt-in run log. With options(pdmS7.run_log = "runs.csv") or PDMS7_RUN_LOG set, every run_pdm() call, and so sim_pdm() and sim_snow_pdm(), appends one row: who, when, an optional tag, the model’s pdm_fingerprint(), a checksum of the forcing, period, versions, run time, and success or the error message. Calibration evaluations, spin-up cycles and the calibration log’s own reruns are not logged. With a register of calibration projects set (pdmS7.register or PDMS7_REGISTER), each run is marked approved, superseded (its project was reopened) or unapproved; runs are never blocked. New read_run_log(), approved_configurations() and pdm_fingerprint(). Logging is off by default and a logging failure never stops a run.
  • New calibration log: an append-only, tamper-evident record of a calibration project. start_calibration_project(), register_data(), select_structure(), log_trial(), log_auto_calibration(), log_note(), propose_candidate(), validate_candidate(), sign_off_project() and reopen_project() each write one YAML entry recording who, when, which data and parameters, the scores and the reasoning. Entries are chained by MD5, data are copied and checksummed, and every run records a checksum of its output. verify_project() detects edits, gaps, changed data and runs that no longer reproduce. A Steward cannot sign off their own calibration. read_project(), project_trials() and read_projects() read the record. Design: calibration-log-design.md.
  • New build_report() writes a calibration report generated from the log: a self-contained HTML file with embedded figures, and a Markdown copy. It shows integrity status first, then data and scoring windows, model structure, the calibration path as a tree and a table, the candidate’s hydrographs, flow-duration curves and scorecard for both windows, parameter sensitivity on a shared scale, sign-off history, and the final configuration. It uses base graphics only.
  • New pdm_scorecard(): NSE, log NSE, KGE and its components, RMSE, signed and absolute volume error, peak error, and the Yilmaz et al. (2008) flow-duration-curve signatures.
  • Five new illustrated articles on the package website: choosing model components, starting states, calibration, forecast updating, and the C core. Articles, guides and the function reference are grouped by topic in the site navigation. DESCRIPTION gains URL and BugReports.
  • calibrate_pdm() gains opt-in multi-start calibration through starts and seed. Start 1 is the configured point; extra starts are drawn uniformly inside the bounds, all are optimised, and the best objective is returned. The result gains start_results, a table of per-start objective, convergence code, evaluation count and fitted parameters. The default starts = 1L runs the same single optimisation as earlier versions.
  • run_pdm(), and so sim_pdm() and calibrate_pdm(), now run a compiled time loop for every capacity distribution; standard, split and demand recharge; and cascade, power-law and exponential stores on either route. It is about 430 times faster. Output agrees with the R loop to rounding: bit-identical on R 4.3, with last-place differences on R 4.5 and later, where calibrated parameters can differ from earlier versions by about 1e-13 relative. options(pdmS7.engine = "r") forces the R loop, which remains the reference implementation. Building from source now needs a compiler (Rtools on Windows); cpp11 is a build-time dependency only.
  • Added inst/benchmarks/time_solvers.R and a report at docs/benchmarks/solver-timing.md timing both solvers and both engines on daily and 15-minute series.
  • pdm_model() (and so pdm_from_config() and sim_pdm()) warns, once per session, when the Smith cubic solver is used with a step above 1 hour. Its error grows with the square of the step and reaches 60 to 100 per cent of peak flow at a daily step. Results are unchanged; the default adaptive solver is unaffected. inst/benchmarks/smith_step_error.R reproduces the evidence.
  • The compiled time loop now sits behind a language-neutral C interface (src/pdm_core.h, interface version 2), so other languages can call the same model code. src/pdm_engine.cpp is a thin R wrapper over it, and results are unchanged. The core validates its own inputs and leaves the caller’s state untouched on error. tools/core/README.md covers building it without R.
  • Golden test files in inst/golden/ hold inputs and expected outputs from the R reference, for checking any binding of the core. tools/core/check_golden.c checks them from plain C.
  • The triangular capacity distribution is now inverted exactly (cube root or the trigonometric solution of a cubic) and the lognormal by safeguarded Newton iteration, in place of uniroot() with a 1e-10 tolerance. Storage round trips improve from about 2e-11 to 1e-14 mm; model outputs for these two distributions change by at most about 3e-11.
  • Fixed: the rectangular distribution’s capacity_mean() used (cmin + cmax) / 2 while its other methods used the Pareto b = 1 form, which can differ in the last place. A soil store filled exactly to capacity could then fail with “Soil storage exceeds capacity_mean”. Both now use the Pareto form, so capacity_mean() can change in the last place.
  • The PACK snowpack also runs in the compiled core, about 540 times faster than its R loop and bit-identical to it on R 4.3. sim_pack() and sim_snow_pdm() use it automatically. The core gains pdm_pack_run() for snow alone and pdm_snow_run() for snow feeding PDM.
  • New initial_state_from_flow(): a warm start in steady state with the flow observed at the start of a run. Routing stores deliver their share of the flow, the soil store is set so that recharge equals baseflow, and delay queues hold the water in transit. It replaces an arbitrary soil fraction for short test runs and forecasts. Also in the core as pdm_state_from_flow().
  • Forecast updating also runs in the compiled core: correct_state() (state correction, Moore 2007 Eq. 28-30) and update_forecast() (ARMA error prediction, Eq. 31-42), with pdm_correct_state() and pdm_update_forecast() for other languages. Results are bit-identical to the R code. Fitting the ARMA coefficients stays in R.
  • The compiled core is now plain C99 (src/pdm_core.c), so other languages need only a C compiler to build it. Results are bit-identical to the previous C++ version.
  • Fixed: the compiled engine rejected an initial state whose values were all stored as integers, for example one read with read.csv(). The R loop accepted it.
  • A peak timing objective is deferred.

pdmS7 0.3.1

  • Added three executable vignettes: PDM equations and functions, PACK snow accounting and defaults, and a synthetic calibration/validation/restart workflow.
  • Added reproducible process diagrams, soil/cover curves and workflow hydrographs.
  • No changes to the numerical model APIs or equations.

pdmS7 0.3.0

  • Added optional PACK S7 snow components, conservative substep accounting, areal depletion, fresh-snow memory and coupled PDM restart.
  • Added the image parameter preset (explicit hourly-unit assumption) and a distinct report-typical preset, with full parameter mapping and source notes.
  • Added multi-objective metrics, weighted multi-start calibration, evaluated Pareto trade-offs, configurable scales and joint snow/PDM parameter paths.
  • Documented river networks and additional state assimilation as future work.

pdmS7 0.2.0

Flode Tier 3 engineering target

  • Introduced Flode-prefixed S7 classes with existing class names retained as aliases.
  • Added sim_pdm() with explicit depth units, integer minute steps, data.table output, UTC timestamps, and warm-up flags.
  • Added safe YAML loading and an illustrative configuration file.
  • Replaced CSV input with fread() and tabular assembly with rbindlist().
  • Added state-object validation and structured debug logging.
  • Converted numerical regression checks to testthat and added interface tests.
  • Added roxygen source documentation, renv, lintr, and pinned shared Flode CI.
  • Retained the earlier simulation functions and output column names for compatibility.

This release targets the Tier 3 technical checks. It is not formally approved for operations: human maintainer attribution, independent review, and catchment validation remain required. Version 0.1.0 serialized S7 objects should be rebuilt from their saved configuration because the canonical class names have changed.
